title: Moneybox Sets Out Six Policy Asks to Bring 7 Million More People Into Stocks and Shares ISAs by 2035
summary:
Moneybox, the award winning wealth management platform with over 2 million customers and £23 billion in assets under administration, has today launched a retail investing manifesto that sets out six key policy asks to take the UK from a nation of savers to a nation of confident investors. 
The manifesto, which was previewed at an exclusive event at One Great George Street on Wednesday 21st October, calls on the government to double down on making investing as easy as saving. If done correctly, the opportunity is significant: 7 million adults have £10,000 or more sitting in cash savings, the real-world illustration of findings from Moneybox’s 2026 Financial Confidence Index that shows confidence in investing (40%) significantly trails confidence in saving (83%). The manifesto argues that closing this confidence gap with practical, behavioural and product-led policy changes could help bring those savers into the stocks and shares ecosystem.
Brian Byrnes, Director of Personal Finance at Moneybox said: “The policy asks in our manifesto are designed to remove the structural and cultural barriers holding people back, creating a clear pathway to bring millions more people into stocks and shares ISAs by 2035. 
“We know that more of our friends, family, and the general public should be investing, and while great strides have been made with the democratisation of access thanks to technology, there is more that can and should be done to ensure people achieve the resilience and security that investing can bring.” 
The six policy asks outlined in the manifesto are:
Build on the success of the Lifetime ISA
Rather than creating new products from scratch, the government should build on the success of the Stocks and Shares Lifetime ISA, a government backed investment product that is growing in popularity every year.
Update the adviser charging rules
Review and modernise the adviser charging rules to allow for more innovative and accessible pricing models for advice, closing the advice gap and helping millions invest with greater confidence.
Launch government-backed investment funds
Establish a range of low-cost diversified funds with a home country bias (similar to Sweden's AP7 Såfa) to provide first-time investors with a clear, confident and sensible entry point to investing.  
Extend workplace auto-enrolment to saving and investing 
Extending workplace auto-enrolment to saving and investing accounts that employees are opted in to. This will remove friction and build long-term investing habits effortlessly.
Provide workplace investment and pension health checks
Make workplace investment and pension health checks more regular, more personalised and easier to access so savers and investors get reassurance that they’re on the right track.
Produce a 10-year retail investing strategy with a government champion
Appoint a dedicated government champion to unite fragmented oversight, establish shared goals, and lead a unified 10-year strategy to grow retail investment.
The launch of Moneybox’s retail investing manifesto also coincides with the 10th anniversary of the launch of its app. Drawing on those 10 years’ of experience, and insights from over 2 million customers, it believes these measures can broaden participation and build investing confidence nationwide.

Ondato and Trinsic Expand Digital Identity Verification Amid EUDI Transition
summary:
Ondato, a compliance technology provider offering an all-in-one platform for identity, risk, and customer journey across IDV/KYC, AML and age verification for regulated businesses, announces a partnership with Trinsic to verify their customers through digital identity. This partnership arrives at a critical time in the EU, as multiple member states roll out  EU Digital Identity Wallets under the European Digital Identity (EUDI) mandate. Trinsic will act as Ondato’s infrastructure provider behind the new digital identity capability.
According to eIDAS 2.0 (Regulation (EU) 2024/1183), all 27 EU member countries must offer at least one digital identity wallet to their citizens by the end of 2026. These digital wallets are designed as government-issued or government-recognised mobile apps that allow an individual to prove their identity and voluntarily share verified information about themselves when interacting with regulated businesses. By December 2027, banks, financial institutions and other regulated businesses that require strong user authentication will be required to accept these wallets when requested by users as a way to verify customers.
Ondato is expanding its capabilities now to prepare for this major development in European digital identity. This builds on the national digital identity methods Ondato already supports, such as Smart-ID. EUDI wallet-based verification will become part of Ondato’s larger customer intelligence platform. As with all of Ondato’s verification options, this functionality will feed into risk scoring, continuous fraud monitoring and detection, and optimising the entire customer journey.
Liudas Kanapienis, co-founder and CEO of Ondato, says, “EU digital identity wallets are the biggest change in a generation to how Europeans prove who they are. For many regulated businesses, accepting them won't be optional. With Trinsic, our clients can accept wallets as they launch, on the same platform they already use for verification, risk and monitoring. It's another step in our expansion as the intelligence layer between businesses and their customers, in Europe and beyond.”
Riley Hughes, CEO of Trinsic, says, “As the leading digital ID gateway for identity verification, Trinsic has been preparing for EUDI since the earliest phase of the mandate. We already support national identity authentication services for France, Italy, Denmark, Austria, and other member states. With this partnership, we’re providing the necessary technology backing for Ondato’s customers amidst the most important European digital ID mandate of the decade.”
Ondato’s EUDI wallet acceptance capabilities will live alongside its existing suite of identity verification and KYC methods. Using Ondato, businesses will continue to utilise a robust roster of digital identity verification tools backed by continuous fraud protection, all available on a single comprehensive platform.

85% of Travel Intermediaries Say FX Cost Is a Challenge, Despite Only One in Four Tracking This Cost
summary:
Modulr, the payments automation platform built to scale, has today revealed exclusive research highlighting the hidden cost of FX for travel intermediaries. The research reveals that, while 85% of travel intermediaries say FX cost is a challenge, only 26% track this cost precisely. 88% of respondents roughly estimate that it is more than €300,000 per year.
The research launches alongside Modulr’s new FX solution featuring account-to-account and virtual card currency exchange, so you can convert on demand with transparent, competitive rates as well as issuing virtual cards in your supplier's currency and funding from your primary balance.
Integrated directly into Modulr’s platform, this gives businesses a single place to convert balances, fund cross-currency card payments, and manage multi-currency operations, with no need for separate FX providers.
When fragmented FX becomes an operational problem
For businesses running multi-currency operations, FX has long meant a separate provider, a separate process, and a separate reconciliation trail, ultimately creating risk. Modulr’s new research, surveying 400 finance, treasury, and operations decision-makers at travel intermediaries across the UK and Western Europe, highlights the real cost of this risk. 93% of respondents, for example, say their business has paid to convert the same money twice, and only 5% have processes to stop it.
Only one third (32%) describe their FX as fully integrated, or handled automatically in the platform they use to pay suppliers. Treasury teams are spending more time managing disconnected systems than optimising payments operations. Costs are often hard to predict, and the burden compounds as transaction volume grows.
Modulr’s integrated FX solution addresses these challenges and reduces operational cost by handling conversion inside the same platform used for payments, accounts, and cards, creating a more automated and streamlined process. Rates are transparent, competitive with the mid-market rate, and consistent at weekends with no surcharge. Businesses pay only the exchange rate margin on each conversion, with no fixed or monthly fees.
Melek Pirgon, Chief Product Officer at Modulr, said: “For businesses scaling across currencies, FX can often mean friction, with a separate provider, a separate reconciliation process, and costs that are hard to predict. The research we have launched today highlights this, with just one quarter of businesses tracking the cost of FX despite 85% citing it as a challenge.
That is one of the key problems we are removing with our FX solution, built directly into the same platform our customers already use for automating payments. This means transparent and competitive rates as well as a full audit trail with no new system or stakeholders to manage. I’m excited to see how we build this offering out in the coming months, including offering booking-linked FX protection to ease the FX cost of booking margins for our customers.”
Looking ahead, Modulr will be expanding its FX solution to offer booking-linked FX protection, helping travel businesses secure exchange rates for future supplier payments and manage the impact of booking changes. By connecting hedging with virtual cards, account-to-account payments and reconciliation, the FX component of booking margins is made much more predictable.

title: Strategic Partnership With Ecommpay Gives Dolphin Dynamics’ Travel Clients Access to Global Payments Platform
summary:
Travel technology provider, Dolphin Dynamics, is working with inclusive global payments provider, Ecommpay, to provide its clients with access to the award-winning payment gateway for local and alternative payment methods in any currency. The strategic partnership also allows travel agents, tour operators and travel management companies (TMCs) to benefit from Ecommpay’s risk and authorisation tooling.
UK-based Dolphin Dynamics provides travel businesses with an integrated suite of CRM, reservations, back-office and booking-engine software designed to reduce daily administration and streamline operational processes. Its platform provides a central environment for managing bookings and associated operational and financial processes. Working with tour operators, leisure travel agencies and TMCs, from independents to multinational corporations, Dolphin Dynamics supports businesses in more than 15 countries.
Through the strategic partnership, Dolphin Dynamics integrates Ecommpay’s payment capabilities with its travel technology platform. Customers completing a payment are directed to Ecommpay’s hosted payment page, where payment information is entered and processed within Ecommpay’s environment. Dolphin then uses Ecommpay’s API to retrieve the payment status, update the booking accordingly and register the payment.
By linking payment activity back into Dolphin, payment status can be reflected within the booking workflow and the corresponding payment registered in Dolphin, helping connect the customer payment journey with the wider booking management process.
“Our aim is to simplify back-office processes for our travel clients, ensuring every stage of the customer journey runs smoothly and without friction,” said Chuck Richardson, Managing Director at Dolphin Dynamics. “To achieve this goal, we carefully select specialists that will deliver fit for purpose solutions.
“Ecommpay delivers secure and accessible payments across borders and in all currencies, allowing our clients’ customers to pay using their preferred payment methods. This boosts conversions and profitability by increasing confidence and convenience and supports a positive booking experience, from research to booking confirmation.”
Roy Blokker of Ecommpay added: “This partnership deepens our footprint within the travel and hospitality sector, where we work with specialist travel-tech providers who need affordable access to multi-currency acceptance and conversion. Our inclusive and accessible payments platform ensures all payments are secure and compliant, regardless of region or currency.
“Dolphin Dynamics helps travel operators of all sizes to optimise processes and grow sales by streamlining back-office systems, and now the payment stage of the checkout journey can run as smoothly as the rest of the experience, without adding complexity for the travel operator.”

Mastercard Expands First-Party Trust Program to Help European Merchants From Rising “Friendly” Fraud
summary:
Mastercard today announced the expansion of its First-Party Trust program across Europe, to address the growing trend in first-party fraud, often referred to as ‘friendly’ fraud. This occurs when a cardholder disputes a legitimate purchase, either intentionally or because they do not recognize the transaction on their statement.
Global chargeback volume is predicted to reach 324 million transactions in 2028, a double-digit increase over the 2025 forecast of 261 million1. As digital commerce continues to grow across Europe, merchants and issuers face increasing pressure to manage disputes efficiently while accurately distinguishing genuine fraud from legitimate purchases.
Mastercard’s First-Party Trust program is designed to support this effort by increasing transaction transparency, through risk model-driven insights to inform authorization decisioning and merchant-provided evidence to assist issuers in reviewing disputed transactions. European issuers will be able to make more informed dispute decisions by more accurately distinguishing third-party fraud from first-party fraud.
How It Works
The First-Party Trust program aims to create greater transaction transparency between issuers and merchants, by giving merchants, including small businesses, the opportunity to submit pertinent insights to counter first-party fraud.
Mastercard provides two paths for the sharing of these enhanced insights between a merchant and card issuer. Merchants can send the insights directly as part of the transaction, or they can do so as part of the disputes process. The program enhances the resolution of such disputes by providing:
First Party Trust insights in authorization, powered by Mastercard fraud models, to help issuers separate third-party fraud, where someone's card details are used without their consent, from first-party fraud. Issuers get fraud-risk signals that point to likely third-party fraud and flag the transactions with the highest levels of trust;
Merchant-provided evidence that supports issuers assess the legitimacy of a disputed transaction, including information associated with the purchase, delivery, and authentication of the transaction, where available and appropriate;
New rules defining compelling evidence that can support issuers with the review of disputed purchases and reduce unnecessary chargebacks, including merchant chargeback protection for disputes that meet First-Party Trust evidence sharing requirements.
Michele Centemero, Executive Vice President, Services Europe, at Mastercard says: “As digital commerce continues to grow, building trust across the ecosystem has never been more important.  By helping merchants and issuers access relevant transaction information needed to review disputed purchases, we can reduce unnecessary disputes while strengthening confidence across the payments ecosystem.”
First-Party Trust is a global program that launched in the U.S., Canada, Latin America, the Caribbean, and across the Asia Pacific region in 2024. It will become available in Eastern Europe, Middle East and Africa in October 2026, and across Europe in July 2027.
NoYesPayments22 Oct, 2026
content: Mastercard has announced the expansion of its First-Party Trust program across Europe to help merchants combat rising first-party or friendly fraud. Set to launch in July 2027, the initiative increases transaction transparency by sharing risk model insights and merchant-provided evidence with issuers. This aims to help accurately distinguish genuine fraud from disputed legitimate purchases, reduce unnecessary chargebacks, and build greater trust across the digital payments ecosystem.

Businesses Expect AI to Manage Over a Third of Corporate Travel Spend by 2028, Worth an Estimated $700bn Globally
summary:
AI is expected to manage or authorise more than a third (37%) of corporate travel spend by 2028, equivalent to $700bn (£535bn) globally when applied to GBTA's 2025 business travel spending forecast. New research from Conferma, a global leader in virtual payment technology, reveals how businesses are preparing to give AI agents greater control over company money, extending their role from booking travel to managing payments.
Across the organisations surveyed, AI is expected to manage or authorise around 37% of corporate travel spend on average by 2028, while 28% expect agents to manage more than half of their travel budgets.
Controls surrounding agentic purchasing are developing more slowly. While 81% of organisations already have some form of policy, control or payment guardrail in place, only 36% describe those controls as comprehensive.
Mark Ledsham, CEO at Conferma, says, “Agentic spending authority is developing faster than the controls around it. Corporate travel could be one of the first proving grounds for agentic payments because it combines high transaction volumes, clear policies and significant spend.
Giving an AI agent authority over company money is very different from using AI to recommend a flight or hotel. Businesses need clear limits on what agents can spend, where they can spend it and when human intervention is required. The controls around those decisions must remain fixed, traceable and accountable.”
Larger travel programmes expect AI to take on more spend
The organisations managing the largest corporate travel budgets expect agents to take on the greatest share of spending. Those spending $6.8 million (£5 million) or more each year on corporate travel expect AI to manage around 51% of their travel spend by 2028, compared with around 27% among those spending less than $136,000 (£100,000).
More than half, 53%, of organisations spending $6.8 million (£5 million) or more say they already have comprehensive AI controls in place. 
As agents gain authority over larger pools of corporate spend, limits, supplier controls, monitoring and auditability become increasingly important.
Senior leaders are more confident than operational teams
Senior leaders are also substantially more willing to give AI autonomy. 86% of executive leaders and heads of department say they trust AI to manage travel bookings and spend, compared with 62% of travel and procurement decision-makers.
However, greater confidence does not mean fewer concerns. 69% of executive leaders and heads of department identify data security as a concern, compared with 59% of finance respondents and 38% across procurement and travel management. Businesses need greater alignment between leadership ambition and the operational controls required to support autonomous purchasing at scale.
Businesses are looking to put controls into the payment itself
Virtual cards rank highest for perceived security in AI-led corporate travel purchasing, selected by 30% of respondents, ahead of digital wallets at 21% and corporate cards and bank transfers at 19% each.
Among organisations with AI purchasing safeguards already in place, 55% require human approval before AI can complete a purchase, 51% use real-time monitoring, 49% apply spending limits and 37% currently use virtual cards with single-use or controlled spending limits.
Use of controlled virtual cards in this group is expected to rise from 37% to 48% by 2028, the biggest expected increase of any safeguard. As businesses prepare for greater agent autonomy, the findings indicate that attention is turning to payment methods that can carry spending rules into individual transactions.
Ledsham added, “As agents become more capable of acting independently, businesses need a way to delegate spending without handing over unrestricted financial authority. Payments can become part of that control layer. A controlled virtual card allows businesses to capture the speed and efficiency of agentic purchasing without removing the financial guardrails around the transaction. 
Corporate travel has the potential to be the testbed for how businesses will manage a much broader transition towards agentic commerce: giving AI enough authority to act while ensuring control over corporate money remains visible, enforceable and accountable.”

content: By 2028, businesses expect artificial intelligence to manage over a third of corporate travel spend globally, reaching an estimated $700bn. Research from Conferma highlights that while senior leaders are confident in granting AI greater purchasing autonomy, organizations are increasingly focusing on robust payment controls, such as virtual cards and spending limits, to ensure financial safety and accountability.
